name: gradient
description: Representative ATen schema, copied verbatim: aten::gradient.scalarint(Tensor self, *, Scalar? spacing=None, int? dim=None, int edge_order=1) -> Tensor[]. This representative signature is representative only and NOT an exclusive ABI. The original Gems pytest owns the full contract: all overloads, keyword arguments, return values, raised errors, aliasing and mutation behavior; never remove tests or adapt reference behavior to fit this one signature. This form is chosen because it is the only registered overload whose non-self arguments are all optional, so it matches the default-only calls torch.ops.aten.gradient(ref_inp) and flag_gems.gradient(inp) that the pytest exercises across many shapes, value ranges, dtypes, non-contiguous strided/permuted views, autograd backward and NaN/Inf scenarios, and the benchmark default case dim=None, spacing=None, edge_order=1. Semantics derived from the tests: numerically differentiate a single tensor, returning a Tensor[] with one tensor per differentiated dimension (list-valued return counts as one logical output); dim may be an int, a list of ints (including negative indices and an empty list meaning no dimension), and defaults to all dimensions; spacing may be a scalar, a list of scalars, or a list of per-dimension coordinate tensors, and defaults to unit spacing; edge_order accepts 1 or 2; each differentiated dimension must have size >= edge_order + 1; non-differentiated size-1 dimensions are allowed; repeated dims, out-of-range dims, invalid edge_order, spacing length mismatch, and spacing tensors that are not 1-D raise errors; unsupported dtypes (uint8, bool, and vendor-specific fp8 on nvidia) raise RuntimeError; for floating and complex inputs the outputs stay in the autograd graph and are differentiable. Other registered schemas, copied verbatim: aten::gradient.scalarint(Tensor self, *, Scalar? spacing=None, int? dim=None, int edge_order=1) -> Tensor[] | aten::gradient.scalararray(Tensor self, *, Scalar spacing, int[] dim, int edge_order=1) -> Tensor[] | aten::gradient.array(Tensor self, *, int[] dim, int edge_order=1) -> Tensor[] | aten::gradient.scalarrayint(Tensor self, *, Scalar[] spacing, int? dim=None, int edge_order=1) -> Tensor[] | aten::gradient.scalarrayarray(Tensor self, *, Scalar[] spacing, int[] dim, int edge_order=1) -> Tensor[] | aten::gradient.tensorarrayint(Tensor self, *, Tensor[] spacing, int? dim=None, int edge_order=1) -> Tensor[] | aten::gradient.tensorarray(Tensor self, *, Tensor[] spacing, int[] dim, int edge_order=1) -> Tensor[]. Scalar/list spacing forms and all error behavior remain owned by pytest, not by this definition.
